exercises.title: Every size in every colour
exercises.problemHtml:
The T-shirt page needs every combination of size (table sz) and color (table col). Return size, color ordered by size then color.

Sample tables: the Notes app of chapters 5–6

app_user  (id PK, name, city)                    1 Cuong Hanoi · 2 Lan Danang · 3 Minh Hanoi · 4 Hoa Hue (no notes)
note      (id PK, user_id → app_user NULL, title, tag NULL, views NULL, pinned)
          1 Intro to SQL (1, sql, 120, pinned) · 2 Indexes (1, sql, 90) · 3 Timezones (2, date, 45) · 4 Backup (3, ops, 12, pinned)
          5 Orphan draft (no user, no tag, views NULL) · 6 JSONB tips (1, sql, 30) · 7 Date math (2, date, views NULL)
note_stat (id PK → note.id, reads)              notes 1–6 (note 7 has no stat row)
comment   (id PK, note_id → note, user_id → app_user, body)   6 comments: 3 on note 1, 1 each on notes 2, 3, 4
employee  (id PK, name, manager_id → employee)  An (boss) ← Binh, Chi · Binh ← Dung, Em · Dung ← Giang
sz (size) S, M, L · col (color) black, white

Full script: the notes-app.sql tab.

Requirements

  • FROM sz CROSS JOIN col.
  • 3 × 2 = 6 rows.

SELECT u.name, n.title
FROM app_user u
LEFT JOIN note n ON n.user_id = u.id
                AND n.tag = 'sql'        -- filter the RIGHT side inside ON: unmatched users survive

exercises.title: Recommend books customers have not bought yet
exercises.problemHtml:
Marketing e-mails customers 1, 2 and 3 a recommendation for every active product of category Giáo trình IT (id 12) they have not bought yet (in any order, whatever its status). Return customer_id, sku ordered by customer_id, sku.

Sample database: CT Shop mini (the course's lab project, sliced)

customer       (id PK, email UNIQUE lower-case, full_name, phone NULL, city DEFAULT 'Hà Nội', created_at timestamptz)
category       (id PK, name UNIQUE, parent_id → category.id — NULL = root)       12 rows: 1–4 roots, 5–12 children
product        (id PK, sku UNIQUE, name, category_id → category, price numeric(12,2) > 0, stock int ≥ 0 DEFAULT 0,
                attrs jsonb DEFAULT '{}', is_active boolean DEFAULT true, created_at)          16 rows (ids 1…46, gaps)
orders         (id PK, customer_id → customer, status pending|paid|shipped|cancelled, created_at timestamptz, note)   14 rows
order_item     (order_id → orders ON DELETE CASCADE, product_id → product, qty > 0, unit_price) — PK (order_id, product_id)
payment        (id PK, order_id UNIQUE → orders, amount, method cod|card|momo|bank, paid_at)    one per paid/shipped order
stock_movement (id PK, product_id → product, change ≠ 0, reason import|sale|return|adjust, order_id NULL, created_at)
review         (id PK, product_id → product, customer_id → customer, rating 1–5, body, created_at) — UNIQUE (product_id, customer_id)

Same 8 tables as Labs 1–9 (in schema public instead of shop); the rows are a small slice of the lab data — same category tree, same product ids/SKUs/prices. Every id is GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY: leave it out of INSERT. Times are timestamptz shown in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Full script: the ctshop.sql tab.

Requirements

  • Candidates = customers {1,2,3} CROSS JOIN active books.
  • Remove the pairs that already appear in that customer's order lines.

-- Plain PostgreSQL: run it as-is in psql to get the same database on your machine.
SET TimeZone = 'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh';
CREATE TABLE customer (
  id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email       text        NOT NULL,
  full_name   text        NOT NULL,
  phone       text,
  city        text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Hà Nội',
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT customer_email_key   UNIQUE (email),
  CONSTRAINT customer_email_check CHECK (email = lower(email) AND email LIKE '%_@_%.__%')
);
CREATE TABLE category (
  id         int  GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  name       text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  parent_id  int  REFERENCES category(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
);
CREATE TABLE product (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  sku          text          NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name         text          NOT NULL,
  category_id  int           NOT NULL REFERENCES category(id),
  price        numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (price > 0),
  stock        int           NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (stock >= 0),
  attrs        jsonb         NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  is_active    boolean       NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at   timestamptz   NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES customer(id),
  status       text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
               CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled')),
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  note         text
);
CREATE TABLE order_item (
  order_id    bigint        NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  product_id  bigint        NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  qty         int           NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0),
  unit_price  numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (unit_price > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id)
);
CREATE TABLE payment (
  id        bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id  bigint        NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES orders(id),
  amount    numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount > 0),
  method    text          NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('cod', 'card', 'momo', 'bank')),
  paid_at   timestamptz   NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE stock_movement (
  id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  change      int         NOT NULL CHECK (change <> 0),
  reason      text        NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('import', 'sale', 'return', 'adjust')),
  order_id    bigint      REFERENCES orders(id),
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE review (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id   bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  customer_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES customer(id),
  rating       smallint    NOT NULL CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  body         text,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (product_id, customer_id)
);

SELECT c.id AS customer_id, p.sku
FROM customer c
CROSS JOIN product p                                  -- every customer × every book …
LEFT JOIN (orders o JOIN order_item oi ON oi.order_id = o.id)
       ON o.customer_id = c.id AND oi.product_id = p.id
WHERE c.id IN (1, 2, 3)
  AND p.category_id = 12 AND p.is_active
  AND oi.order_id IS NULL                             -- … minus what they already bought
ORDER BY c.id, p.sku;

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: CROSS JOIN builds the full candidate set on purpose; the anti-join then removes what already exists. Joining orders and order_item together (in parentheses, or with NOT EXISTS) makes "this customer bought this product" one test, avoiding the fan-out of the second wrong answer.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: CROSS JOIN cố ý dựng đủ tập ứng viên; anti-join rồi bỏ những gì đã có. Nối orders với order_item thành một khối (trong ngoặc, hoặc dùng NOT EXISTS) khiến "khách này đã mua sản phẩm này" là một phép thử duy nhất, tránh nhân dòng của đáp án sai thứ hai.

solutionCodeJson.code:
# Name the join trap — answer key

1. SELECT … FROM orders, customer WHERE orders.status = 'paid' returns 6 000 rows for 750 paid orders and 8 customers.SELECT … FROM orders, customer WHERE orders.status = 'paid' trả 6 000 dòng cho 750 đơn đã trả và 8 khách.
   Answer: a) an accidental cross join: no join condition
   750 × 8 = 6 000: every paid order paired with every customer. The comma syntax makes a forgotten condition easy — write explicit JOIN … ON.VI: 750 × 8 = 6 000: mọi đơn đã trả ghép với mọi khách. Cú pháp dấu phẩy dễ quên điều kiện — hãy viết JOIN … ON tường minh.

2. Revenue per customer doubles after you add JOIN order_item to a query that sums payment.amount.Doanh thu theo khách tăng gấp đôi sau khi thêm JOIN order_item vào truy vấn cộng payment.amount.
   Answer: a) fan-out: the payment row repeats once per line
   A one-to-many join multiplies the "one" side. Sum amounts before joining the lines (chapter 6.4).VI: Phép nối một–nhiều nhân bản phía "một". Cộng tiền trước khi nối với dòng đơn (bài 6.4).

3. A LEFT JOIN report "every customer and their paid orders" suddenly lost the customers with no paid order.Báo cáo LEFT JOIN "mọi khách và đơn đã trả của họ" bỗng mất các khách chưa có đơn đã trả.
   Answer: b) the status filter was written in WHERE, not in ON
   WHERE o.status = 'paid' rejects the NULL rows the LEFT JOIN kept. Move it into ON.VI: WHERE o.status = 'paid' loại những dòng NULL mà LEFT JOIN vừa giữ. Chuyển nó vào ON.

4. Joining notes to users with ON u.name = n.author_name shows some notes twice.Nối ghi chú với user bằng ON u.name = n.author_name làm vài ghi chú hiện hai lần.
   Answer: c) the join key is not unique: two users share a name
   A join is safe when one side is unique (a key). Names are not unique — join on ids.VI: Phép nối an toàn khi một phía là duy nhất (một khoá). Tên không duy nhất — hãy nối theo id.
